top.logout.title: Unpair this device
top.logout.confirm: Unpair this device? You will need to scan the QR code again.
chart.temp.title: Temperatures · last 10 min
chart.temp.aria: CPU and GPU temperature over the last 10 minutes
chart.rpm.title: Fans · RPM · last 10 min
chart.rpm.aria: Motherboard fan RPM over the last 10 minutes
chart.rpm.noFans: This motherboard reports no fans to FanPilot.
chart.rpm.none: No fan is reporting RPM right now.
chart.rpm.silent: No RPM reading (0): {fans}. They are left out of the chart.
fans.title: Motherboard fans
fans.sub: tap a fan to adjust it
fans.softwareCurves: On this board FanPilot runs the curves: when it closes, the fans go back to BIOS control.
fans.unsupported: This motherboard ({board}) has no fan control through the path FanPilot uses.
turbo.banner: Turbo is on: every motherboard fan at 100% (the GPU is not affected). Tap again to go back to the previous settings.
profiles.afterTurbo: Takes effect when Turbo goes off
response.fast.desc: follows the temperature almost at once and slows down after cooling 1 °C.
response.balanced.desc: ignores spikes of a few seconds and only slows down after cooling 2 °C.
response.smooth.desc: ignores spikes of about 10 s, changes speed slowly and only slows down after cooling 4 °C.
orphan.text: The settings saved for "{name}" match no fan on this board and were not applied.
ed.turboOn: Turn Turbo off to adjust a single fan.
ed.profileNote: The {profile} profile is on: applying or restoring here turns it off, and the other fans keep its curve as their own setting.
ed.fixedHint.chip: Protection: the chip still goes to 100% if the sensor goes above {temp} °C.
ed.fixedHint.app: Protection: FanPilot still goes to 100% if the sensor goes above {temp} °C.
ed.limits: At least {min}% at any point; 100% at {max} °C at the latest.
ed.limits.chip: The curve runs in the motherboard's chip (it keeps working even if the PC or FanPilot closes).
ed.limits.app: FanPilot runs the curve every second. If it closes, or the reference sensor stops answering, the fan goes back to BIOS control.
ed.limits.socket: The curve follows the board's sensor (its "CPU" is the socket one); the CPU card shows the cores' temperature.
ed.response.hint: {name}: {desc} With any response, at the curve's last point the fan goes to 100% at once.
ed.applied.app: Applied: FanPilot is controlling this fan
ed.restored.bios: Fan handed back to BIOS control
ed.discard.question: Discard changes?
ed.discard.text: What you changed here hasn't been applied yet.
ed.points.aria: Curve points: drag them, or use the arrow keys
ed.tune.hint: Tap a point to adjust it one step at a time. With a keyboard: Tab to the point and use the arrow keys (with Shift, 5 at a time).
ed.tune.label: Point {i} of {n}: {t} °C, {p}%
ed.pumpNote: Protected pump: anything applied here becomes 100%. To allow another speed, change the protection under "Name and role".
ed.meta.name: Name
ed.meta.hint: The name shows on the panel and the charts, with the original next to it. On a pump, nothing FanPilot applies goes below the protection: not the editor, not Turbo, not a profile.
gpu.safety: {n}% · back to automatic at {temp} °C or more
alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.settings: Limits and notifications outside the panel
alerts.privacy: Nothing leaves the PC without a destination here, and the messages carry only the alert and the PC's name. The ntfy address and the token are kept encrypted on this PC; a field left blank keeps what is already saved.
pair.title: Pair a phone
pair.scan: Scan it with the phone's camera (on the same Wi-Fi network). The code works once and changes every few minutes.
pair.firewall: If the phone can't connect: allow the port in the firewall (scripts\firewall.ps1) and check that the Windows network is set to "Private".
locked.title: 🔒 Device not paired
locked.how: On the PC, open {url} (it opens by itself when FanPilot starts) and scan the QR code with this device's camera.
locked.hint: The QR code lasts a few minutes and works only once.
